title: A _root.md or pointer that is not valid UTF-8 passes publish's tree refusal and the sync range gate, since blobs() drops undecodable files
goal: An unreadable _root.md or pointer counts as not public in tree_refusals, history_refusals and internal_prefixes, and the tree cause says it could not be read

import sys,os,subprocess as s,tempfile
sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import kbpublic as k
d=tempfile.mkdtemp();g=lambda *a:s.run(['git','-C',d,*a],check=True,capture_output=True)
rev=lambda:s.run(['git','-C',d,'rev-parse','HEAD'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.strip()
g('init','-q')
def w(p,t):
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(d+'/'+p),exist_ok=True);open(d+'/'+p,'wb').write(t)
def cm(m):
    g('add','-A');g('-c','user.name=t','-c','user.email=t'+chr(64)+'example.com','commit','-qm',m);return rev()
w('a',b'x\n');b0=cm('base')
w('kb/team/_root.md',b'---\nroot: team\nid_prefix: T\nvisibility: public\ndescription: x\xb3\n---\n');w('kb/team/a.md',b'x\n');cm('team')
f=k.tree_files('HEAD',d)
t=k.tree_refusals('HEAD',f,d);h=k.history_refusals('HEAD',b0,f,d,projected=False)[0];p=k.internal_prefixes('HEAD',f,d)
print(t,h,p)
sys.exit(0 if t and h and 'kb/team/' in p and any('read' in x for x in t) else 1)

clauses.clause: An unreadable _root.md or pointer counts as not public in tree_refusals, history_refusals and internal_prefixes
the tree cause says it could not be read

notes: Review gap G2 of SP-n7zxspch. kbpublic.py:510-512 and :515-518 read through blobs()/texts() (:454-457), which drop undecodable blobs; history_refusals :860-866 and :879-882 and internal_prefixes :620-623 do the same. A cp1250 byte in a Polish description is enough. kbcommon.load_root raises UnicodeDecodeError on such a file (not RootError), so other tools fail on it while publish and sync pass it. Premise run 2026-11-09: the repro fails on the base (an undecodable _root.md gives no tree cause). Outbound paths: tree_refusals and history_refusals serve publish (shipped=True) and the sync range gate; internal_prefixes serves tree_hits (the tracked-file scan test_leaks and bl_check read), so one fix in kbpublic.py covers all of them; the planted check plants an undecodable _root.md that says visibility: public and asks all three functions. An unreadable file counts as not public (the closed rule), so no exemption is added.
